title: The band refuses to record unless Sarah Vaughan records her first song
summary: When the label wants to drop Sarah's tune, she cries, the band says nobody records without her, and Eckstine wins the point.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The recording director, the record company guys were there, and they called Billy up into the office they had there for some kind of discussion. So we're taking a break, and we're smoking and whatever. So Billy comes back out; he's got this very solemn look on this face. He says, "Fellows, come on. Gather around." So we gathered around. He says, "Something's come up. Instead of recording Sarah's tune, the tune that she's going to sing, 'I'll Wait and Pray,' they would like for me to do another blues and have Sarah record this on the next record date." So nobody smiled or did anything.

All of a sudden, Sarah began to cry, since this is her first record date, and what these people are thinking about is makin' some money, and they're ignoring Sarah altogether. So Sarah began to cry. And to show you how close the band was, how tight and how much they cared about Sarah, everybody said, "Well, if Sarah don't record, then nobody's going to record.
We're not going to record anything else." And I think Billy was relieved to hear this. So he didn't argue the point at all...

As I was saying, Billy didn't argue the point at all. He just turned around and went back and told these guys how we were thinking. So he came back out with a smile on his face, and said, "We're going to do Sarah's tune." And we did Sarah's tune. It was a beautiful tune called "I'll Wait And Pray," an original by Jerry Valentine, who did most of the arranging -- all of it except for my "Opus X."
